classification.difficultyReason: Justify the angle using parallel north lines and apply cosine rule to the two sailing legs.

content.prompt:
A ship sails 53 nautical miles from $P$ to $Q$ on a bearing of $026^\circ\mathrm{T}$.
It then sails 78 nautical miles due east from $Q$ to $R$.

spec.description: P lower left, Q above-right, R horizontally right of Q. Black triangle, dashed north arrow at P extending above Q, 26° with a leader into the narrow bearing angle, 53 Nm inside beside PQ and 78 Nm above QR. No north line at Q.
spec.mathematics: PQ=53 nautical miles on bearing 026°; QR=78 nautical miles due east. PR is unlabelled.

answer.short: Draw a north–south line at $Q$. Alternate angles give $26^\circ$ between $QP$ and south, so $\angle PQR=90^\circ+26^\circ=116^\circ$.
answer.worked: Draw a north–south line through $Q$, parallel to the north line at $P$. The angle between $QP$ and south is $26^\circ$ by alternate angles. Since $QR$ is due east, $\angle PQR=90^\circ+26^\circ=116^\circ$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How far apart are $P$ and $R$, correct to the nearest nautical mile?
